To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the median time of viral shedding was 4 days, the median time of fever was 0.5 days, the median duration of cough was 2 days, and 34% of infections were asymptomatic.
influenza virus shedding peaks on day 2 after infection and lasts 4.8 days, fever is present in 37% of cases, and symptoms are present in 67% of cases.

viral shedding increases sharply on day 1, peaks on day 2 and is over on day 4; that fever is rare, but systemic symptoms are common, that the frequency of symptomatic and asymptomatic infections are 67% and 33%, and that respiratory symptoms are more frequent than systemic symptoms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of mathematical models for the transmission of infectious diseases.
the natural history of influenza virus infection, a key parameter for the evaluation of epidemic control strategies.

the development and application of new methods for the analysis of infectious disease data, including time series analysis, spatial statistics, and statistical methods for the analysis and modeling of longitudinal data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
influenza virus infection in healthy adults is characterized by a short period of viral shedding and a short period of symptoms.

influenza virus shedding peaks at day 2 and is prolonged for 5 days, that 1 in 3 persons are asymptomatic and that 2 out of 3 persons with symptomatic infection experience fever and 1 in 2 experience respiratory symptoms.
the duration of viral and symptom shedding is similar for A/H1N, A/H3N and B viruses, but the frequency of symptomatic illness is higher for influenza B virus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the duration of viral shed is about 5 days, and that 1/4 of infected people are asymptomatic, and that 2/3 of infected people have symptoms, with the majority having respiratory symptoms and about 1/3 having fever.
the dynamics of viral infection in humans are very similar to those observed in animal models.
the duration of viral infection and shedding is similar for all influenza A subtypes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamics of viral and symptoms shedding are similar for all subtypes and strains of influenza virus tested.
the dynamics of viral load and symptoms following infection with influenza virus are similar in healthy adults, regardless of influenza A or B subtype.
the duration of viral sheding and the frequency of fever are not significantly different in A/H1N2 and A/H3N1 infections.
